subject.title: bug: Duplicate messages sent to Slack

question: Can a maintainer or operator inspect the named Slack session's gateway logs and Slack message IDs to determine whether the duplicate is a known fixed class or a still-current delivery bug?
rationale: The repo source shows adjacent guards, but only operator-side logs can distinguish OpenClaw double-send from Slack API retry, streaming fallback, or a different channel delivery path for this exact session.

options.title: Inspect Named Session Logs
options.body: Use the session key, gateway delivery logs, and Slack message timestamps/IDs to map the duplicate to a concrete source path before deciding whether to fix or close.

options.title: Wait For Reporter Evidence
options.body: Keep the issue marked needs-info and ask for redacted Slack message IDs, timestamps, version, and a log excerpt if operator logs are not accessible.

options.title: Close After Stale Info Window
options.body: If no maintainer logs or reporter evidence arrive after the stale-insufficient-info window applies, close with a request for a fresh actionable report.

recommendation.title: Inspect Named Session Logs
recommendation.body: Use the session key, gateway delivery logs, and Slack message timestamps/IDs to map the duplicate to a concrete source path before deciding whether to fix or close.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history on the Slack duplicate preview/fallback path and appears frequently in the relevant Slack dispatch and reply-dedupe history.
